narrative.summary: The OIC's AI text recorded here is the International Islamic Fiqh Academy's resolution on artificial intelligence (2025). It is non-binding.

instruments.official_title: Resolution No. 258 (3/26): Artificial Intelligence: Its Rulings, Guidelines, and Ethics
instruments.english_title: International Islamic Fiqh Academy Resolution No. 258 (3/26) on Artificial Intelligence: Its Rulings, Guidelines, and Ethics
instruments.issuing_authority: Council of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy of the OIC, 26th session
instruments.publisher_name: Council of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy of the OIC, 26th session
instruments.summary: Jurisprudential resolution on AI. It holds that developing and using AI is permissible subject to six conditions: lawful purpose, use, funding and outcomes; bringing benefit and preventing harm; not insulting beliefs, religions or religious symbols; protecting information and public and private rights and freedoms; not threatening individual, societal or national security; and upholding honesty, documentation and transparency. It recommends further study of whether AI can be given legal personality and specialised symposiums on AI ethics.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Council of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy of the OIC at its 26th session in Doha, State of Qatar (4–8 May 2025); published on the Academy's site on 20 November 2025.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read on the IIFA official site. Session printed as Doha, Dhul-Qi'dah 1446H (4–8 May 2025); the page also carries a post date of 20 November 2025. Month of adoption used. Arabic original presumably on iifa-aifi.org/ar (not opened). | Independent check 2026-10-21: Resolution No. 258 (3/26), title, 26th session in Doha, Qatar (Dhul-Qi'dah 1446H, 4-8 May 2025), issuer 'Council of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation', six conditions and two recommendations confirmed on iifa-aifi.org (page dated 20 November 2025).; current_status: the page does not call the IIFA a 'subsidiary organ' of the OIC nor say the text is not binding on states.

leads.note: Not checked; count only if adopted by OIC member states. Update 2026-11-08: the COMSTECH Ten-Year STI Strategic Plan ('Building Bridges and Nurturing Scientific Talent'; https://comstech.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/COMTSECH-Ten-Year-STI-Strategic-Plan-20-sep-2023.pdf), prepared for the 2nd COMSTECH Scientific Advisory Council meeting (Islamabad, 12-13 June 2023), treats AI as a sub-area under research, teaching and innovation rather than a pillar and names no approving body; an institutional science plan, not recorded.

leads.title: Tehran Declaration, 2nd Ministerial Meeting of the OIC-15 Dialogue Platform (Tehran, 19-20 May 2025), theme 'Trustworthy and Ethical AI for Sustainable Development'
leads.note: OIC news page of 19 May 2025 says 'The meeting concluded by adopting the Tehran Declaration', on innovation in science and technology through AI. Press reports describe an AI cooperation framework (education, research, AI governance and ethical standards, public-private partnerships, technology transfer, talent mobility, start-ups). OIC-15 is a 15-member platform, so the declaration would apply only to its participants, not to all OIC members. No official full text found.
